about: Task 19's operator form, converter self-consistency on public models (WNTR's bundled ky4 and ky10, rewritten by fixtures.py), never a test on a utility's own files: ky4's clean drawing completed by a form built from the original, against the pre-registered bars; ky10's PRVs restored and its boundary valve closed by the form, against the original; the refusals. Written by python -m residualmap.intake_exp form.

skeleton_blocking: No reservoir, inflow junction or tank found: the model needs a place where water enters.
form_blocking: No water source: the form has no source row, so the model has nowhere for water (and chlorine) to enter and cannot run. Add a source row: the node at the plant, well or zone inlet, and the hydraulic grade it holds (head_ft).

age_note_without_rows: 3 pipes of the skeleton take Hazen-Williams C from their material alone (new-pipe values, or 130 where the map names none), so a decades-old cast iron main gets more than a new ductile iron one, and the model's old-pipe factor, which scales wall decay by C, cannot see the pipe's age. Give your own C for each material (pipe_c rows) if you have them. The 2 pipes whose C the layer's own C field gives keep it.

notes: The model's clock starts at 08:00: the form's pattern, given from midnight, is shifted so each clock hour keeps its multiplier.

grammar_fuzz.what: the final verifier's grammar fuzzer, seed 11, 3,000 random well-formed forms, as its console gave it; a completed model is counted 'disconnected' when EPANET's 24 h report names a node disconnected
grammar_fuzz.left: a tank on the only path to a branch, low enough to fill, fills to its maximum and then closes, so EPANET cuts the branch off: when a tank fills or empties is not checked

files_given_as_the_form.an EPANET model: This file is an EPANET model (.inp): 25 EPANET sections found in the first 64 KB, text in utf-8. The operator form is a table: CSV, or an Excel workbook (.xlsx). It is a model, not the form: the form is a table, one row per item (a source, a tank, a pump and so on), that completes a model. On the command line the model comes first and the form second.
files_given_as_the_form.a DXF drawing: This file is a CAD drawing (DXF, text): group codes and values. The operator form is a table: CSV, or an Excel workbook (.xlsx). It is a map of the mains, not the form: the form is a table, one row per item (a source, a tank, a pump and so on), that completes the model built from the map (on the command line, cad_read or gis_read with --form, the map first and the form after --form).
files_given_as_the_form.a GeoJSON layer: This file is a GIS layer (GeoJSON): 5 features, lon/lat coordinates (WGS84). The operator form is a table: CSV, or an Excel workbook (.xlsx). It is a map of the mains, not the form: the form is a table, one row per item (a source, a tank, a pump and so on), that completes the model built from the map (on the command line, cad_read or gis_read with --form, the map first and the form after --form).

a DXF drawing.refused: This file is a CAD drawing (DXF, text): group codes and values. This command completes an EPANET model (.inp). A drawing is completed by its own command, which keeps each pipe's material and the drawing's coordinates: python -m residualmap.cad_read DRAWING.dxf --form FORM.csv --out completed.inp.

a GeoJSON layer.refused: This file is a GIS layer (GeoJSON): 5 features, lon/lat coordinates (WGS84). This command completes an EPANET model (.inp). A GIS layer is completed by its own command, which keeps each pipe's material and the layer's coordinates: python -m residualmap.gis_read LAYER --form FORM.csv --out completed.inp (a GeoPackage, a zipped shapefile, GeoJSON, KML or KMZ).

a form.refused: This file is a table in text form (CSV or similar): separated by commas; first row: kind, id, location, pipe, upstream, head_ft, dose_mgL, residual_mgL. This command completes an EPANET model (.inp): give the model first and the form second.
